key_insight: The Hankel Neural Operator (HNO) combines rational-kernel convolution with finite-rank boundary corrections to learn differential-equation solution operators beyond periodic Fourier representations.
engineering_relevance: HNO offers a promising surrogate for fluid and transport simulations where boundaries, persistent dynamics, and grid refinement challenge Fourier-based models.
method: Decomposes linear constant-coefficient boundary-value solution operators into Toeplitz and finite-rank Hankel-type components.
Implements non-periodic FFT convolution, including a causal form, and closed-loop dynamics without fading memory.
Provides a rational Fourier multiplier formulation containing FNO as a special case.
evidence_signal: HNO achieved the lowest mean test error across nine LNO benchmarks and three FNO benchmarks; six ODE errors improved 2.1–5.2× over the better baseline, while Darcy error stayed nearly constant from 85² to 421² grids.
watch_item: The structural theorem covers well-posed linear constant-coefficient problems on an interval, and some reported benchmark improvements were not statistically significant.
paper_title: Beyond Fourier and Laplace: The Hankel Neural Operator for Learning Solution Operators of Differential Equations
